item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Tshisekedi’s 2024 record is mixed but somewhat pro-stability on the narrow macro side. The strongest evidence shows IMF-backed stabilization, no monetary financing, reserve accumulation, and a real push to tighten treasury and expenditure controls. The weak points are slower-than-planned reform execution, persistent inflation/deficit pressure, and still-fragile long-term investment conditions.

**Accepted Claims**
- [IMF Executive Board Concludes the 2024 Article IV Consultation and Completes the Sixth Review under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for the Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr) | IMF | 2024-07-03 | The IMF said the authorities kept prudent macro policies, continued to avoid monetary financing, and made progress on revenue mobilization and reserve build-up. It also warned that public-finance reform was slower than planned and inflation remained elevated. | `5B.3` | Evidence ID: `E0337`

- [IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with the Democratic Republic of Congo on an Extended Credit Facility and a Resilience and Sustainability Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf) | IMF | 2024-11-13 | The new IMF package was explicitly framed around inclusive growth, diversification, job creation, governance, and poverty reduction, with tighter spending-chain discipline, treasury reforms, and insulation of spending from volatile extractive revenues. | `5B.3` | Evidence ID: `E0338`

- [Ministère du Budget: Coopération RD Congo-FMI](https://budget.gouv.cd/ministere-du-budget-cooperation-rd-congo-fmi/) | Ministère du Budget | 2024-11-15 | The budget ministry said the finance and budget ministers jointly negotiated the new IMF programs and that better coordination of fiscal and monetary policy had been in place since June 2024. This is strong evidence that the economic team was being empowered to execute stabilization policy. | `5B.3` | Evidence ID: `E0341`

- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Congo, Democratic Republic of: April 2024 - Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099434404082425237) | World Bank | 2024-04-03 | The World Bank said growth prospects were favorable, but fiscal and current-account deficits, currency pressure, and inflation would persist unless much more ambitious reforms were adopted. This is the clearest counterweight to the IMF optimism. | `5B.3` | Evidence ID: `E0328`

- [DRC president Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said public resources were being squandered, essential social services were underfunded, and mining expansion was driving forced evictions and pollution. That points to weak long-term investment conditions and weak conversion of resource wealth into broad-based development. | `5B.3` | Evidence ID: `E0330`

- [Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts: report](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-45741663/) | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement, which is indirect but relevant evidence against fiscal responsibility and transparent public-finance management. | `5B.3` | Evidence ID: `E0329`

**Search Gap**
I found solid primary evidence on macro stabilization and IMF-linked reform, but not direct 2024 evidence that Tshisekedi materially strengthened central-bank independence, produced durable inflation relief, or clearly improved private investment conditions by year-end. The positive case is mostly policy design and coordination; outcome evidence is thinner.
